Several competitions leak test labels, making scores trivial

release.quote: Code for the paper ["MLE-Bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07095). We have released the code used to construct the dataset, the evaluation logic, as well as the agents we evaluated for this benchmark.

redistribution_questions: The external Kaggle competition datasets and files downloaded while using this package are not covered by the repository licence, so their terms and redistribution rights must be checked separately.
Kaggle credentials (kaggle.json) are needed to download the raw datasets, so use of the data is bound by the Kaggle API/account terms.
Some MLE-bench competition data is stored using Git-LFS (git lfs fetch --all; git lfs pull).
rights.quote: NOTE: This license applies to the code in this repository, but not the external datasets and files that may be downloaded while using this package.

tasks.quote: The MLE-bench dataset is a collection of 75 Kaggle competitions which we use to evaluate the ML engineering capabilities of AI systems.

verifier.full_credit: A CSV submission graded above the medal threshold for that competition, scored as the any_medal_percentage metric.
verifier.quote: Given a JSONL file, where each line corresponds with a submission for one competition, `mlebench grade` will produce a grading report for each competition.

oracle.path: competition.answers (answers loaded by mlebench/grade.py via load_answers)
oracle.quote: For each competition, we also provide grading scripts that can be used to evaluate the score of a submission.

exceptions: Some MLE-bench competition data is stored using Git-LFS
runtime.quote: Agent resources - not a strict requirement of the benchmark but please report if you stray from these defaults! Runtime: 24 hours; Compute: 36 vCPUs with 440GB RAM and one 24GB A10 GPU

questions: Which split is the target: the 22-competition Low/Lite set or the full 75-competition set?
How will Kaggle credentials and dataset downloads be handled inside the container without network surprises?
Where do the held-out answers and grading server live so agents cannot see them?
How are agent runs launched (run_agent.py plus agent start.sh) and how long and how much GPU may they use?
readiness.next_action: Install the package, run `mlebench prepare --lite`, and grade one sample submission with `mlebench grade-sample <PATH_TO_SUBMISSION> spaceship-titanic` to confirm the verifier works.
